title: Not my first air fryer, its OK
text:
Not my first air fryer, its OK. Maybe I'm just spoiled because I'm comparing this to an air fryer that I already love, but I found this one to be sub-optimal.
Air fryers, if you are unaware, are basically small high powered convection ovens that can simulate the effect of "frying" on certain types of food (like french fries). To do this, you need precise temperature controls and timing, since it happens rather quickly (a difference of a minute or two in the machine is significant). So one of the first things that turned me off to this one is the fact that the timer is a manual dial that WON'T LET YOU ADJUST THE TIME once you've set it. In other words, if you overcrank the time (say, to 10 min instead of 7), you can't turn it back down. You have to just wait out that amount of time until it finishes. That's a silly oversight if you ask me. My other air fryer, for contrast, has a digital display for the timer which can be adjusted at any time during the process. This one? You have to unplug it if you don't want it to continue running for the time you accidentally set.
Also the slotted tray insert comes out of the drawer rather easily, but the plastic tabs need to be lined up again for it to go back in (you have to push it with your thumb to slide it back into the open position). Just a silly nuisance that could have been avoided since I know other air fryers at similar price points don't have this issue.
As far as the food, it DOES work, as long as you preheat it first. And the first time you use it, of course, you should let it burn out for 30 min to avoid new appliance smell on your food. It's an alright air fryer, especially if you get it for a bargain sale price, but otherwise I feel like there are better models on the market with less quirks.
